description: The line plot illustrates the sparsity ratio of SDPA (Scaled Dot-Product Attention) output across different layers of a large language model, under a threshold of 1e-3, as described in the paper “Gated Attention for Large Language Models: Non-linearity, Sparsity, and Attention-Sink-Free.” The x-axis, labeled “Layer,” spans from 0 to approximately 22, representing the depth of the model’s transformer layers, with tick marks at regular integer intervals. The y-axis, labeled “Sparsity Ratio,” ranges from 0.0 to 0.8 and is linearly scaled, indicating the proportion of attention weights pruned below the threshold. Three distinct lines are plotted: a blue dashed line labeled “sparsity ratio before gate, avg 0.003,” which remains near zero across all layers, indicating minimal sparsity prior to gating; an orange dotted line labeled “sparsity ratio after gate, avg 0.126,” which starts near 0.8 at layer 0, drops sharply to below 0.2 by layer 5, and continues to decline gradually to near 0.03 by layer 22; and a green dash-dot line labeled “sparsity ratio after average gate, avg 0.080,” which begins near 0.75 at layer 0, drops steeply to below 0.1 by layer 5, and then declines more gradually to approximately 0.01 by layer 22. All three lines converge near zero sparsity in later layers, but the “after gate” condition consistently exhibits higher sparsity than the “after average gate” condition across most layers.
